items.title: feat(atlas): stage code/config artifacts as embedding entries — item writer + atlas-stage ingest (#1518)
items.body: Refs #1518, #2469. Queue task 17164 (second landing; the confirmed definition landed in PR #10350). ## What this adds: the item writer (minimal ingestion path, staging tier) The #1518 design doc (doc/2026-11-14T19-00-00Z_design_code-config-embeddings.md, §6) sequences the first ingestion as: stage one `items` row + `chunks_raw` into an Atlas staging unit, promote (embedding at promotion), then prove semantic retrieval. Until now no code wrote `items`/`chunks_raw` rows at all. This PR builds the writer: - `atlas_core::stage::stage_artifact` (+ `stage_artifact_in_db`): stages one repository artifact into a v1 staging DB as one `items` row plus its `chunks_raw`, exactly per the confirmed definition — `source` carries the source-of-truth pointer (`repo:path@commit_sha`); `meta` carries the required metadata set (repo, path, commit_sha, kind, language, unit, embedded_at, chunks); sensitivity is the existing basic classification, recorded on the row. The DB must pass `check_stage_schema` first; a non-staging DB is refused. - Unit rules from the definition: at or below 32 KiB the whole file is one unit (`unit: whole-file`); above it, `chunk_artifact_text` splits into declaration-sized chunks (breaks before top-level declaration lines, 64 KiB hard ceiling split at line boundaries). Chunks always partition the input exactly — concatenating them reproduces the artifact byte for byte — and each chunk's `content_hash` is its SHA-256. - `atlas_core::stage::list_staged_items` (+ `_in_db`): read-back of staged items with chunk counts. - CLI: `atlas-stage ingest --db … --unit … --repo … --path … --file … --commit … [--kind] [--language] [--sensitivity]` and `atlas-stage items --db … [--unit …]`. ## First entry staged (proof at the staging tier) On the laptop, against a fresh staging unit (`task-17164`): - `atlas-stage provision` → unit open, schema v1 - `atlas-stage ingest` of `infra/dns/dns_config.yaml` (31,264 bytes, at commit d85bd4ff1f3b73700f881aa99357adeae997e1bd) → `item_id 1` - `atlas-stage items` read-back: kind `config`, source `developing-today/code:infra/dns/dns_config.yaml@d85bd4ff…`, unit `whole-file`, 1 chunk, full metadata — the #2469 artifact is now staged as the first code/config entry. ## Tests 3 new oracle tests in `stage::tests` (staged rows read back from a real provisioned DB): whole-file staging with exact metadata + hash-verified chunk; large-config declaration chunking with the lossless-partition oracle (200 records → 200 chunks, concat == input); refusal on a non-staging DB. `cargo test -p atlas-core` — 126 lib tests pass; `cargo test -p atlas-search` passes (41 + 11). Changed files are `cargo fmt` clean (pre-existing fmt drift in manifest.rs was left untouched). ## What remains on task 17164 (recorded, not in this PR) Promotion/embedding of the staged unit (the aggregator slice of #5669 — `Registry::promote` is gated on the #7648 embedding-model contract), the live semantic-retrieval proof against the promoted index, and the shard-size benchmarks the design sequences after retrieval is proven. Task 17164 stays open with these as its next steps; #2469 stays open until the promoted index actually returns the config. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: Split actor.rs and edge.ts under the production line limit
items.body: Part of #14547. Pure structural split — moves only, no behaviour change. Both files named by the production-line guard are back under the 2500-line limit, and no file was added to the grandfather list. ## Layout **pkgs/id (id-worlds)** — `world/actor/command.rs` is new: the `WorldCommand` enum and its `name()` move out of `world/actor.rs`, which re-exports it (`pub(crate) use command::WorldCommand`), so the `world::actor::WorldCommand` path every caller uses is unchanged. | file | before | after (production lines) | | --- | --- | --- | | crates/id-worlds/src/world/actor.rs | 2562 (4386 raw) | 2082 (3906 raw) | | crates/id-worlds/src/world/actor/command.rs | — | 495 | **pm-stack console edge** — two new modules beside `edge.ts`: - `edge-shared.ts`: the shared constants and shapes, the pure held-action helpers (`withMachine`/`heldAbout`/`insertHeld`), and `Mirrors`, the store of the host's section copies (it takes the edge's `ready`/`confirmed` as injected functions, so nothing about when sections settle changes). - `release.ts`: `Builds` — the released Android build and the copy kept at the edge, including `noteBuild`, which is the sync path's take-in of a build report, moved verbatim. `Edge` delegates; the fetch/health call sites read `builds.releaseTrouble` for what was `released?.trouble`. `edge.ts` re-exports `KV`, `EdgeOptions`, `SILENT_MS`, `LIVE_MS` and `next` for its existing importers (the test suite imports `Edge`, `KV` and `SILENT_MS` from it). One local had to be renamed: `heldWaits`/`heldMine` each declared a Set called `withMachine`, which as a method name was unambiguous but shadows the imported helper in its own initializer — the local is `machineAbouts` now. | file | before | after | | --- | --- | --- | | edge/src/edge.ts | 2975 | 2469 | | edge/src/edge-shared.ts | — | 345 | | edge/src/release.ts | — | 288 | edge.ts lands at 2469, 31 lines under the limit — noted so the next growth there knows the headroom is thin. ## Verification (remote, fleet-command on developing-today/fleet) - Production line guard, run 45468931888 (head cb0c6cb2f): `production-line-guard: OK` — 1066 .rs and 292 .ts files checked; only the three pre-existing grandfathered warnings (#8891, #13051, #13052). `rustfmt --check` on both split .rs files clean in the same run. (A package-wide `cargo fmt --check -p id-worlds` also flags pre-existing drift in untouched files — program_registry_pkarr.rs, journal.rs, world/mod.rs, world_session/* — present on main; not touched here.) - Console suite, run 45470448962 (head dfba14652): **660 pass / 0 fail across 26 files**, and `tsc --noEmit -p ../tsconfig.json` clean (via bunx; the executor image has no node/npm — dezren39/fleet#111 — so `npm ci` could not be used; `bun install` provided the type-check tools). - id-worlds suite, run 45467530232 (head 78a9b5b56): **1016 passed / 0 failed**. A re-run on the final head dfba14652 (run 45471249805) was dispatched to remove any doubt; the only pkgs/id delta after 78a9b5b56 is the rustfmt seam commit (mod order + blank lines). No new dependencies. items.title: test(atlas): add DNS source retrieval fixture
items.body: ## Summary ```text pkgs/atlas-search/ ├── fixtures/dns-search-corpus.sql # isolated DNS source document ├── fixtures/dns-search-spec.json # fixed toy query/document vectors └── crates/atlas-core/tests/parity.rs # vector retrieval assertion ``` Adds an explicit `infra/dns/dns_config.yaml` retrieval fixture. The production Atlas corpus is external and is a personal-conversation corpus, not a code-document manifest; this PR does not mutate it or claim production ingestion. Existing code#6025 (queued task 13656) tracks first-pass ingestion of repository documents. Issue #2469 remains open for that production follow-up; this PR references rather than auto-closes it. ## Evidence - **Before:** no Atlas fixture named the DNS source or asserted retrieval of its MX record. **After:** the fixture query `Which MX host handles mail for 01b.us?` returns `infra/dns/dns_config.yaml` with `monday.mxrouting.net` through the vector-search path. - `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/atlas-search/Cargo.toml -p atlas-core` — 42 unit, 6 parity, 11 shard, and 6 stage tests passed. - `rustfmt --check --edition 2024 pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-core/tests/parity.rs` and `git diff --check` pass. Workspace `cargo fmt --all --check` still reports pre-existing formatting drift in untouched `crates/atlas-embed/tests/gate_a.rs`. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way — test-fixture-only change, revertible without production data changes. **Blast Radius:** low — isolated `atlas-core` parity fixture. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: doc(atlas): code/config embeddings — confirmed definition, verdict, qualifying criteria (#1518)
items.body: ## Summary First landing for task 17164 / issue #1518 (confirmed code/config embeddings design; Drew confirmed the recommended design 2026-11-12, ledger `embedding-ranking-1518`): the written definition the issue's done-criteria require. The doc records, grounded in the current Atlas staging schema (`pkgs/atlas-search/schema/atlas_stage_v1.sql`): - **Definition** — unit of embedding (whole file for small configs, declaration-sized chunks for large configs/code), the required metadata set (repo, path, commit SHA, kind, language, embedded_at, unit, sensitivity, source-of-truth pointer), and freshness (commit-triggered re-embedding, stale marking by SHA mismatch, eviction on delete). - **Same-dump verdict** — one Atlas index, entries discriminated by `kind`, kind-aware retrieval quotas; reasons, and why the split arguments are handled inside the shared index instead. - **The three decisions, each naming the failure it accepts** (per the follow-on's acceptance): shared-index pollution risk, whole-file precision loss, and the stale-marking freshness window. - **Qualifying criteria** — infrastructure-defining configs qualify by default; secret-bearing/generated/vendored exclusions; only the existing basic sensitivity filters. - **Drew's added guidance** (allow for more; build into Atlas; sharding to many Turso DBs via workers/DO/D1; benchmark shard sizes) and the sequenced minimal first ingestion: `infra/dns/dns_config.yaml` staged → promoted → semantic-retrieval proof, coordinated with #2469. The ingestion build itself (item writer against `atlas_core::stage`, promotion/embedding run, retrieval proof, shard benchmarks) remains on task 17164, which stays open with the exact next steps recorded. Refs #1518. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(atlas): aggregator embed-at-promotion — staged unit to core scan shard (#1518, #5669)
items.body: ## What The staging aggregator's embed-at-promotion step (#5669 aggregator slice; the sequenced remainder of #1518 after the definition in #10350 and the item writer in #10788): - **`atlas_core::aggregate::embed_unit_into_shard`** — reads one staging unit's `items` + `chunks_raw`, embeds every chunk document-side with the mandated model, writes one new local core scan shard (`atlas-core---.db` with the exact `chunks` / vec-table / `atlas_manifest` schema shard discovery and the fan-out scan already read), stamps the unit DB's `atlas_manifest` `embedding_model`, and promotes the unit through `Registry::promote` — whose M6 gate (#7648, now closed) re-reads the stamp. No new read path: promoted entries are searchable by the existing fan-out. - **`DocEmbedder`** (embed.rs) — the document-side twin of `QueryEmbedder`: prompt-free, stored as produced, per the corpus contract in embed.rs's module docs. `AtlasEmbedder::embed_doc_raw` + `FixedDocEmbedder` included. - **`atlas-stage promote`** CLI verb — production wiring: builds the real embedder with the same model/ORT resolution as the atlas-search binary (ATLAS_MODEL_DIR / ATLAS_ORT_LIB, state-dir / HF-cache snapshots), loud failure when absent. - Chunk sensitivity is written in the scan vocabulary via the tier mapping (`shareable`/`personal`/`secret-bearing`, the inverse of `TierCeiling::from_sensitivity`), so an internal unit's chunks are admitted under the default personal ceiling. Failure shape: embed/write failures before the stamp remove any partial shard and leave the unit open; the stamp closes the staging DB to further `stage_artifact` writes (exact v1 table-set check), matching merge-on-close. ## Tests - New oracle suite `crates/atlas-core/tests/aggregate.rs` (3 tests): promotion of a staged unit (DNS config + prose) into a shard that `open_from_spec("dir:…")` discovers and `fanout_scan` ranks correctly (DNS chunk first for a DNS-shaped query); the registry gate refuses before the aggregator runs; empty-unit and second-run refusals; tier→sensitivity mapping. - `cargo test -p atlas-core -p atlas-search`: all green (126 lib tests + every integration suite, incl. the 3 new ones). `cargo fmt` applied to the touched files only. - Clippy via the shared broker target dir fails with a pre-existing rustc-version mismatch in cached crates (E0514 on serde/serde_json/sha2) — environment artifact, not this change; CI for this workspace is tests-only. ## Remaining on #1518 (recorded, sequenced) Live promotion run against the real model + retrieval proof on #1518, shard-size benchmarks, and closing/linking #2469 — landing in the same task 17164 shift as follow-on steps after this PR merges (promotion needs the merged verb). Refs #1518, #5669. Part of task 17164. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: id(boards): reject duplicate first listings per host

labels.name: audit:no-issue
labels.description: No spawning issue; judged on stated intent

items.body: ## Summary ```text on(BoardListing, supersedes=None) require version == 1 reject if graph already has a listing for this board + host ``` Adds the same-host existence check and regression coverage for duplicate published/withdrawn first listings, while allowing another host's first listing. ## Evidence - **Before:** the existing validation checked only `version == 1`; issue #4109's probe confirmed a second v1 listing was accepted. - **After:** regression test added for both `listed` values and a different-host control. Local `cargo test -j4 -p id --lib listing` could not reach tests: compilation fails in untouched `src/references.rs` (`StoreId: Default` and `rest` lifetime errors), reproduced with this change absent. - **CI coverage:** `.github/ci-policy.md` assigns `id` a PR tier, but `.github/workflows/id-check.yml` has no `pull_request` trigger (only push-to-main, schedule, and dispatch); the PR-tier check is therefore not triggered for this PR. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way; validation-only change, reversible by reverting this PR. **Blast Radius:** low; only rejects malformed chain-less duplicate listings for the same board and host. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Board listings without a superseding reference are now rejected when a listing for the same board and host already exists, including withdrawn listings. * First-time listings for a different host remain accepted.
